findings.title: Count includes every project, not just billable ones (likely overbilling)
findings.explanation: The query counts all rows in `projects` for the org, with no filter on state. The neighboring `activeProjectNames` is named for active projects, so `projects` probably has a column such as `archived_at`, `deleted_at` or `status` that it filters on. The diff doesn't show that query, so please confirm. If such a column exists, archived, deleted or soft-deleted projects would be billed, and this number feeds the invoice generator. Define what 'billable' means with product/billing, then apply the same predicate here. Ideally share one predicate or constant with `activeProjectNames` so the two can't drift apart.

findings.title: Billing semantics are undocumented and no tests are included
findings.explanation: The comment 'one billable unit per project' doesn't say which projects count (archived, trial, free-tier, demo or internal projects) or when the count is taken. A billing figure also needs a point-in-time rule, such as the count at period end, the peak, or a time-weighted figure. A raw current count can differ from what the customer used during the billing period. Please document the rule and add tests covering active, archived and deleted projects, and an org with zero projects.

findings.title: Function is not scoped to the Business plan
findings.explanation: The comment says 'Business plan', but the function takes any `orgId` and does not check the plan. Either make it clear that the caller must check the plan, or rename or document it so it isn't used for other plans by mistake.
